title: Senior Systems Architect
description: Overview DecisionPoint Corporation is seeking a Senior Systems Architect to lead the architecture, integration, implementation, and sustainment of mission-critical Department of Defense (DoD)/Department of War (DoW) enterprise systems operating within secure AWS GovCloud environments. Duties & Responsibilities Lead the design, implementation, and sustainment of enterprise applications and infrastructure solutions hosted within AWS GovCloud IL4/IL5 environments. Develop and maintain logical, physical, application, data, and security architectures aligned with DoD requirements and enterprise architecture frameworks. Provide technical leadership for cloud engineering, platform operations, infrastructure modernization, configuration management, and release management activities. Establish architecture standards, technology roadmaps, and engineering best practices supporting secure, scalable, and resilient operations. Lead architecture reviews, technical design sessions, and stakeholder engagements with government customers and executive leadership. Develop and maintain architecture artifacts, system diagrams, technical documentation, and implementation plans. Ensure compliance with DoD cybersecurity requirements, Zero Trust principles, and cloud security standards. Identify and mitigate technical risks related to architecture, performance, security, data management, and system integration. Mentor technical staff and provide leadership across multidisciplinary engineering and operations teams. Effectively communicate complex technical concepts, recommendations, and architectural decisions to both technical and non-technical audiences. Qualifications Clearance Active Secret security clearance required. Education Bachelor's degree in Computer Sci

title: Sr Vault Engineer
description: Purpose This plan captures what an IBM HashiCorp Resident Architect (RSA) would do to move Synopsys from per-team namespaces to a self-service, pattern-based Vault onboarding model. It is based on the recommendations from the June 5 and June 26 working sessions with the Synopsys Vault team. An RSA is onboarded into your environment as a contractor and builds alongside your Vault team, typically for a short engagement of around 3 months part-time. Current state Synopsys has been running Vault for about a year, with a few teams in production and many in dev. Onboarding is automated for namespace creation only. Everything after that falls to each team. Namespace model: Root namespace, then an admin namespace, then one namespace per team or application group. Teams receive namespace-level admin and manage their own auth methods, policies and secret engines. Onboarding flow: ServiceNow request, then the Vault team adds namespace and user details to Terraform and pushes the change, which triggers the pipeline that creates the namespace and policies. Teams then configure Vault themselves through the CLI, UI or code, guided by an internal wiki. Consumers: GitHub Actions and Azure DevOps pipelines, plus Kubernetes pods. Human users authenticate through Okta. Organization: No central platform team. Application teams have their own DevOps and infrastructure engineers. Challenges raised by the team Many consuming teams are new to Vault and need significant hands-on help to integrate. Vault team effort grows with every team onboarded. Page 1 of 4 Synopsys Vault Adoption: Recommended RSA Engagement Plan Teams on different CI platforms (Azure DevOps, GitHub, others) can't easily share the same modules. No clear path to change models without disrupting teams already in flight. Recommended target state The target is a model where the Vault team's onboarding work is approving a request, and a new team reaches its first secret in minutes. Namespace model: The root namespace is reserved for platform administration. Application teams onboard into a shared namespace and are isolated from each other by ACL policies, not by separate namespaces. Additional namespaces are used only for business-unit or operating-team boundaries. Consumption patterns: Two or three packaged, end-to-end onboarding paths that cover most use cases, built highest impact first. For Synopsys, the likely patterns are: GitHub Actions pipelines, JWT/OIDC auth, KV secrets Azure DevOps pipelines, JWT/OIDC auth, KV secrets Kubernetes pods, service account auth, KV secrets Okta for human access to manage each team's secrets Self-service onboarding: A central onboarding repo in Azure DevOps. A team opens a pull request with a short request file listing team name, application ID, distribution email, Okta groups and pipeline or workload identities. The Vault team approves, and Terraform provisions roles, policies and secret paths. Welcome output: Each onboarded team gets generated instructions covering log

Ability to distinguish subtle differences in Australian and New Zealand English pronunciation and vocabulary, including differences between the two varieties. It includes physical, mental and spiritual well-being for individuals, families and communities. We acknowledge and respect different definitions of wellness and health within our communities. Community Accountability and Empowerment - Communities are the experts on their own health and essential participants in the health of their communities, families and selves. Our services and programs are informed by and responsive to community voices. Diversity as Strength - AA and NHPI communities are rich in diversity of language, cultural heritage, spirituality, history, experience, health beliefs and practices. Many have undergone the hardships of war, colonization, poverty, or immigration to a foreign land. We honor and value the strengths of every culture and individual. Collaboration Among Communities of Color – Communities of color share a history of disparities and exclusion as well as a common interest in health and health care equity. Through collaboration, we learn from each other and grow stronger, while overcoming distrust and divisions that are fostered by competition for limited resource. Kurz gesagt: Wir verbinden Chips zu leistungsstarken und energieeffizienten Netzwerken und überwinden damit bestehende Grenzen der Konnektivität in der Halbleiterindustrie. Wir liefern die Graphenlösung. About the company: 

In the coming decades, demand for critical minerals such as copper, lithium, and cobalt will continue to grow. These minerals are needed to build electric infrastructure, vehicles, data centers, and electronics. However, the mining industry is making 10x fewer discoveries per dollar spent on exploration compared to 30 years ago because the easy-to-find, near surface deposits have largely been discovered.

KoBold was founded to be the first AI native mineral exploration, mine development, and technology development company. Our goal is to turn mineral exploration into a repeatable science to discover the minerals the world needs—by integrating artificial intelligence, human intelligence, and new technology. Our multidisciplinary teams of data scientists, engineers, and geologists work together to build data systems, design new sensors, and establish industry-leading workflows to develop and test subsurface predictions on our exploration projects.

Our first discovery, Mingomba, is a high-grade copper deposit in Zambia, found after spending materially less than industry average. We are developing Mingomba with the same technical rigor that we apply to exploration. The Mingomba team brings together mine and processing engineers, geologists, data scientists, software engineers, and community, health & safety, construction, and operations specialists. By combining industry knowledge and cutting edge technology, we are developing Mingomba into a world class project that has safer and more predictable outcomes for ourselves, partners, and communities. It is expected to create thousands of good jobs for generations.

KoBold runs exploration programs in eight countries, all with the potential for another discovery.

KoBold is privately held; investors include institutional asset managers T. Rowe Price and Canada Pension Plan Investments; technology venture capitalists Andreessen Horowitz, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, BOND Capital, Durable Capital, StepStone, and Standard Investments; and strategic natural resources companies BHP and Mitsubishi.

We are hiring Software Engineers to accelerate our mission.
